senses.en: the way in which a person or group lives, including their habits, work and interests
examples: City life and country life are two very different **lifestyles**.
He changed his **lifestyle** and started cycling to work.
A healthy **lifestyle** includes sleep as well as exercise.

lifestyle.note: Written as one word. Careful: *lifestyle* is how you live; *life* is the fact of living.

senses.en: following ideas, customs or methods that have existed for a long time
examples: They still follow a **traditional** way of life.
**Traditional** houses here are built of wood.
She prefers **traditional** music to pop.

senses.en: of the present time, or using the newest ideas and technology
examples: **Modern** life moves much faster.
The village now has a **modern** school.
He prefers **modern** furniture to antiques.

forms.ex: The government plans to **modernise** the railway.

senses.en: involving a lot of sitting and little exercise
examples: A **sedentary** lifestyle is bad for your health.
Office work is often **sedentary**.
Too much screen time makes children **sedentary**.

senses.en: doing a lot of physical exercise or many activities
senses.vi: năng động, tích cực vận động
examples: My grandfather is still very **active** at eighty.
Try to stay **active** during the holidays.
She leads an **active** life.

forms.en: a thing that you do, often for enjoyment

senses.en: connected with the countryside rather than the town
examples: **Rural** life is quieter but there are fewer jobs.
Many families have moved away from **rural** areas.
The school serves five **rural** villages.

senses.en: connected with a town or city
senses.vi: thuộc về thành thị, đô thị
examples: **Urban** areas are growing quickly.
**Urban** life offers more choice but less space.
Air quality is worse in **urban** districts.

senses.en: far away from towns and places where most people live
examples: They live in a **remote** village in the mountains.
The island is too **remote** for daily ferries.
Teachers are hard to find in **remote** areas.

senses.en: done from a distance, especially using a computer or the internet
examples: **Remote** learning became normal during the pandemic.
She has a **remote** job and works from home.

senses.en: all the people who live in the same area, or a group who share the same interests
examples: The whole **community** helped rebuild the bridge.
She is an active member of the local **community**.
The festival brings the **community** together.

senses.en: all the people in a family or society who are about the same age
examples: The older **generation** prefers the traditional way.
Each **generation** lives a little differently.
Three **generations** share this house.

senses.en: to change your behaviour so that you can deal with a new situation
examples: It took him a year to **adapt to** city life.
Children **adapt** more quickly than adults.
Wildlife must **adapt** as the climate changes.

senses.en: to change something so that it is suitable for a new use
senses.vi: sửa đổi cho phù hợp, chuyển thể
examples: The house was **adapted** for wheelchair users.
The novel has been **adapted** for television.

forms.en: able to change to suit new conditions

adapt.note: Do not confuse **adapt** (change to fit) with *adopt* (take on or take in).

senses.en: to keep something in its original state so that it is not lost or damaged
examples: The village wants to **preserve** its traditions.
These forests must be **preserved** for the future.
The old town has been carefully **preserved**.

senses.en: to treat food so that it can be kept for a long time
examples: Salt is used to **preserve** the fish.
Fruit can be **preserved** in sugar.

forms.en: the act of keeping something safe or unchanged

preserve.note: Compare **conserve** (use carefully so it is not wasted) with **preserve** (keep unchanged).

senses.en: to chase and kill wild animals for food or sport
examples: The Inuit traditionally **hunted** seals for food.
It is illegal to **hunt** these birds.
They **hunt** with dogs in winter.

senses.en: to search hard for something
examples: I spent an hour **hunting for** my keys.
She is **hunting for** a summer job.

senses.en: a vehicle with long narrow strips instead of wheels, used for travelling over snow
examples: Dogs pull the **sled** across the ice.
They loaded the **sled** with supplies.
The children have a small wooden **sled**.

sled.note: Also **sledge** in British English; *sled* is more common in American English.

senses.en: the activity of hunting whales
examples: **Whaling** is now banned in most countries.
The town's economy once depended on **whaling**.
Commercial **whaling** has almost stopped.

senses.en: a small useful tool or device, especially a clever new one
senses.vi: đồ dùng công nghệ nhỏ, thiết bị tiện ích
examples: His kitchen is full of **gadgets**.
This little **gadget** peels garlic in seconds.
Teenagers spend a lot of money on **gadgets**.

gadget.note: Slightly informal. A **gadget** is small and often clever or novel; a *device* is the more neutral, general word.

senses.en: the amount of time you spend looking at a phone, computer or television
senses.vi: thời gian sử dụng màn hình
examples: My parents limit my **screen time** on school nights.
Too much **screen time** can affect your sleep.
She tracks her **screen time** with an app.

senses.en: the state of being healthy, comfortable and happy
senses.vi: sức khoẻ và hạnh phúc, sự an lạc
examples: Exercise improves both health and **well-being**.
The school cares about students' **well-being**.
Sleep has a big effect on mental **well-being**.

well-being.note: Usually hyphenated in British English (*well-being*); Americans often write *wellbeing* or *well being*. Uncountable.

senses.en: to make something continue in the same way as before, so that it does not weaken or disappear
examples: The villagers work hard to **maintain** their traditional lifestyle.
Only a few families still **maintain** the old weaving skills.
It is not easy to **maintain** a friendship across two countries.

senses.en: to keep a machine, road or building in good condition by repairing and checking it
examples: Someone has to **maintain** the village bridge every spring.
The bikes are cheap to **maintain**.

forms.en: the work of keeping something in good condition
forms.ex: The school pays for the **maintenance** of the sports field.

maintain.note: Careful with the stress and the spelling: the verb is main-**TAIN**, but the noun is **MAIN**-te-nance — and it has an *e*, not *ai*, in the middle.

senses.en: to bring back something from the past that had almost disappeared
examples: A group of students is trying to **revive** the old folk songs.
The festival was **revived** after forty years.
Museums cannot **revive** a language; only speakers can.

senses.en: to become strong, healthy or conscious again, or to make someone do so
examples: The flowers **revived** as soon as we watered them.
Cold water on the face soon **revived** him.

revive.note: **Revive** always points at something that was already there and faded. You *revive* an old dance; you *start* a new one.

senses.en: belonging to a group of families who share a language, a place and the same customs
senses.vi: thuộc bộ tộc, thuộc bộ lạc
examples: We watched a **tribal** dance at the village festival.
Each group has its own **tribal** patterns and colours.
**Tribal** drumming can be heard across the valley at night.

forms.en: a group of people of the same origin living together under a leader
forms.ex: Several **tribes** share the same river valley.

tribal.note: Adjective only — you say *a **tribal** dance*, never *a tribe dance*.

senses.en: moving from place to place instead of living in one fixed home, usually with animals
senses.vi: du mục, nay đây mai đó
examples: Some families in Mongolia still lead a **nomadic** life.
**Nomadic** herders follow the grass from valley to valley.
Their **nomadic** lifestyle changes with the seasons.

forms.en: a member of a group that moves from place to place
forms.ex: The **nomads** pack their tents in a single morning.

nomadic.note: Stress the middle syllable: no-**MAD**-ic. The noun **nomad** stresses the first: **NO**-mad.

senses.en: painting, carving and decorated craft made by the first people of a place, in their own style
examples: The museum has a fine collection of **native art**.
You can buy **native art** in the village gallery.
Much of the **native art** here is carved from bone or wood.

native art.note: **Native** here means *of the first people of a place*. In *my native language* it means something else — the language you grew up speaking.

senses.en: the craft of making cloth by passing threads over and under each other
examples: **Weaving** is taught to the girls of the village by their grandmothers.
The **weaving** on this scarf took three weeks.
She sells her **weaving** at the Sunday market.

forms.en: to make cloth by crossing threads over and under each other
forms.ex: They **weave** these threads into beautiful clothes.
The **weaver** works at a wooden loom.

senses.en: a vehicle with no wheels that a team of dogs pulls across snow and ice
senses.vi: xe trượt tuyết do chó kéo
examples: The **dogsled** is still used as a means of transport in Alaska today.
Eight dogs pull the **dogsled** across the frozen river.
We loaded the **dogsled** with food for six days.

dogsled.note: Written as one word in American English, and often as **dog sled** in British English. The sport itself is called *dog sledding* or *mushing*.

senses.en: a person who drives a team of dogs pulling a sled
senses.vi: người điều khiển xe chó kéo
examples: **Mushers** from all over the world come to the race each March.
A good **musher** knows every dog in the team by name.
The **musher** stands at the back and calls to the dogs.

forms.en: to travel over snow on a sled pulled by dogs
forms.ex: They **mushed** for eleven hours without stopping.

musher.note: Nothing to do with *mushy* food. The word comes from the shout drivers once used to start the dogs.

senses.en: a round shelter built from blocks of hard snow
examples: Will they stay in an **igloo** when they visit Alaska?
An **igloo** stays surprisingly warm inside.
Hunters could build an **igloo** in about an hour.

igloo.note: Plural **igloos**. It is a shelter for a night or two on a journey, not the year-round home that films often suggest.

senses.en: something that most people in a place do, so that nobody finds it unusual
examples: Buying breakfast on the street is **common practice** in this city.
Taking off your shoes indoors is **common practice** here.
It has become **common practice** to send an invitation by phone.
colloc: it is common practice to do something

common practice.note: Usually with no article: *It is **common practice** here.* With *a* it means one particular custom: *a **common practice** among students*. **Practice** is the noun; **practise** is the verb in British English.

senses.grammar: be + in the habit of + V-ing
senses.en: used to say that someone regularly does something, because they have done it many times before
examples: My mum is **in the habit of** keeping the kitchen bright and clean.
Many adults here are **in the habit of** having breakfast outside their homes.
I am not **in the habit of** checking my phone at the table.
colloc: be in the habit of doing something
get in the habit of doing something

forms.en: something you do often and almost without thinking
forms.ex: Reading before bed is a good **habit**.

in the habit of.note: Always **V-ing** after *of*: ✅ *in the habit of **getting** up early*, ❌ *in the habit of get up early*.

senses.en: ready-to-eat food or drink sold from a stall or cart in a street or other public place
examples: People here buy and sell a lot of **street food**.
**Street food** is cheap, quick and often better than a restaurant meal.
The best **street food** in our town is sold before seven in the morning.

street food.note: Uncountable: *some **street food***, never *a street food*. For one item, say *a street food dish* or name it.

senses.en: forming the main and regular part of what people eat or use
examples: Rice is the **staple** food in most of Viet Nam.
Maize is a **staple** crop in parts of Africa.
Bread and potatoes were the **staple** diet here for centuries.

senses.en: a food that people eat very often and depend on
examples: Rice and fish are the two **staples** of the region.
Noodles are a **staple** in her kitchen.

staple.note: A different word from the small piece of metal that holds paper together, which is spelled the same way.

senses.en: to say hello to someone, or to welcome them, in words or with a movement
examples: Handshaking, bowing and hugging are ways people **greet** one another.
In Japan people **greet** each other by bowing.
She **greeted** us at the door with a wide smile.

forms.en: the words or action you use when you meet someone
forms.ex: A handshake is the commonest **greeting** in the world.

greet.note: Transitive — it needs an object: ✅ *She **greeted** me.* ❌ *She greeted.*

senses.en: the words or the action you use when you meet someone
examples: Shaking hands is probably the commonest **greeting** in the world.
Pressing noses together is the traditional Maori **greeting**.
A bow is a **greeting** that needs no words at all.

senses.en: friendly words sent to someone in a message or on a card
examples: Send my **greetings** to your grandmother.
The card carried **greetings** from the whole class.

senses.en: to talk to other people and work or spend time together with them
senses.vi: tương tác, giao tiếp qua lại
examples: Mai wants to go to class because she likes to **interact with** her teachers and friends.
Online, students **interact** far less than they think.
Small children learn to **interact** by playing together.

forms.en: the act of talking to and working with other people
forms.ex: A screen gives you no real **interaction**.

forms.en: allowing information to pass both ways between a person and a machine

senses.en: the effect that one thing has on another, especially a strong one
examples: The talk was about the **impact** of modern technology on our lifestyles.
Screen time has a real **impact** on sleep.
The new road had a huge **impact** on the village.
colloc: the impact of something on something

senses.en: the force of one object hitting another
examples: The glass broke on **impact** with the floor.
The **impact** bent the front wheel.

impact.note: The noun stresses the first syllable (**IM**-pact); the verb stresses the second (im-**PACT**). Use **on**, not *to*: *an impact **on** learning*.

senses.en: not connected to the internet; done in person rather than through a screen
senses.vi: ngoại tuyến, không qua mạng, trực tiếp
examples: We had two **offline** lessons a week and three online ones.
My phone was **offline** all weekend and I did not miss it.
Some friendships only really work **offline**.

offline.note: Opposite: **online**. In Vietnamese classrooms *học offline* means the face-to-face lesson, and English uses the word the same way here.

senses.en: to do or feel something yourself, rather than hear about it
examples: Visitors can **experience** some of the local culture in the villages.
I **experienced** real cold for the first time that winter.
You cannot **experience** a festival through a screen.

senses.en: something that happens to you and that you remember
examples: Riding a dogsled was an **experience** I will never forget.
The trip was a wonderful **experience** for the whole class.

senses.en: the knowledge and skill you get from doing something over a long time
examples: She has years of **experience** as a weaver.
He got the job because of his **experience**, not his marks.

forms.en: having a lot of skill from doing something for a long time
forms.ex: An **experienced** musher reads the ice easily.

experience.note: Countable when it means one event (*a strange **experience***); uncountable when it means skill (*five years' **experience***, never *five experiences*).

senses.en: able to do things and make decisions without help from other people
examples: Online learning makes some students far more **independent**.
She has been **independent** since she was fifteen.
My little brother wants to be **independent** and walk to school alone.

senses.en: not controlled or paid for by another country, organisation or person
senses.vi: độc lập (về chính trị, tổ chức)
examples: The country became **independent** in 1945.
It is a small **independent** bookshop, not part of a chain.

forms.en: the state of being free from the control of others
forms.ex: Living away from home gave her real **independence**.

forms.en: without help or control from others
forms.ex: The class worked **independently** for twenty minutes.

independent.note: Spelled with **-ent**, not *-ant*, and the opposite is **dependent** — which is spelled *-ent* too.
